descriptor.scene: THE BIG PICTURE OF THE BOOK. and the GLOWING ORANGE TRANSLUCENT LAPTOP in front of him opens onto A WHOLE LINE OF STATIONS RECEDING DEEP INTO THE SCREEN. At each station a sub-agent works on one thing and passes it on: the first decides who is in the book, the next locks a character sheet, the next draws a spread, the next the cover, the last carries a finished bound book toward the front of the screen. The Chief of Agents stands mid-line with one nub arm raised, directing. THE ENTIRE FACTORY IS INSIDE THE SCREEN and none of it is in the room. Marcus is outside it, watching, and the scale difference between the small tired man and the deep bright line is the point of the composition. CAMERA: THIS IS AN OVER-THE-SHOULDER SHOT. The camera sits BEHIND AND SLIGHTLY ABOVE MARCUS, who is SEATED IN HIS CHAIR at the desk. We look PAST THE BACK OF HIS HEAD AND ONE SHOULDER, which occupy the near foreground at the lower left, straight at the glowing screen, so the viewer sees exactly what he sees. HIS FACE IS NOT VISIBLE AT ALL: we see the back of his head, his dark hair greying at the temples with the wire-rimmed glasses pushed up into it, and the shoulder of his soft OLIVE-GREEN shirt. He is NOT turned toward the camera and NOT seen from the side. The screen is the subject and should hold the centre of the frame. His head and shoulder are small and dark in the near foreground and the bright line receding inside the screen dominates the frame. The scale difference between the small dark shoulder and the deep bright line is the point of the composition. SCALE, and this is the correction: the laptop is a SMALL ORDINARY 14-INCH NOTEBOOK on the desk, its open screen only about twice the height of the mug beside it. The line of stations gets its grandeur from DEPTH, receding far away inside a small screen like a lit corridor seen through a doorway, NOT from the screen being large. Do NOT enlarge the laptop to fit the factory in.
